items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
PDL-CAS-26-013, Council Conference Policy Update
notes:
Regional Clerk, Tim Brubacher, provided an introduction to the report. 

Committee inquired into the conference limits section of the policy; specifically, why significant costs is not defined in the policy. T. Brubacher explained that the policy does not define significant costs on purpose; this allows for some level of interpretation for professional development that the Region may not know of, or exist, yet.

items.title: COR-CFN-26-020, 2026 Mid Year Report
notes:
Commissioner, Resident Experience, Strategy and Communications, Connie MacDonald, and Commissioner of Corporate Services and CFO, Wayne Steffler, provided a presentation. A copy is attached to the agenda.

Committee inquired into the line item listed as "Build Waterloo Region". Staff confirmed that that capital project is just a change in the appraised value of certain employment lands in the Region.

Committee looked for further information on the percentage of the tax levy that the Region is spending on provincial responsibilities. W. Steffler informed committee that the amount and percentage hasn't been updated since late last year. Staff confirmed that the amount spent was roughly $270 million which would be an estimated 25% of the tax levy. Committee commented around how much municipalities spend on provincial responsibilities and the need for a coordinated response and lobbying of the province.

Committee inquired into how the next capital budget will be built; specifically, if it will be built around demonstrated delivery capacity. W. Steffler explained that staff do examine that when they create their projections for the capital budget.

Committee asked for further details on what the external violence against paramedics initiative is and its purpose. Staff confirmed that paramedic staff semi-frequently encounter experiences that make them feel unsafe. This initiative is to provide them with training to help deal with these situations. A semi-annual update report is tentatively scheduled to come forward in September.

items.title: Councillor D. Craig
notes:
Councillor Craig presented his motion to committee.

Committee inquired into how staff would implement this request. W. Steffler confirmed that staff already consider and use some affordability metrics but that some data is not available and staff would have to go externally to find and present the data.

Discussion occurred over how affordability is an important topic for residents of the Region. Discussion also occurred over balancing the need to provide services for the public as well as ensuring that the tax levy is affordable for residents.

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2026 Mid-Year Update as set out in report COR-CFN-26-020 dated August 11, 2026:

  1. Receive the 2026 Mid-Year Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Strategic Plan 2023-2027; and
  2. Amend the 2026 Capital Budget for various capital projects as set out in Appendix D.

motions.text: That the previous question be called.

Whereas municipal property taxes continue to represent a continual and growing expense for households, businesses, and and seniors living on fixed incomes, And whereas, inflation is only one measure of affordability and does not fully reflect residents’ financial circumstances or their ability to absorb additional tax increases, And whereas, the true ability to pay is influenced by household income growth, housing costs, utility costs, food prices, transportation expenses and others cost of living pressures, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: Regional Council direct staff to develop and implement a “Household Affordability Framework” to be included annually as part of the Region’s budgeting process, And that, the framework include where practical : Medium household income trends within the Region of Waterloo; Property tax burden as a percentage of household incomes; Cost of living indicators including housing, utilities, food, transportation, and insurance costs; Affordably impacts on seniors and residents living on fixed incomes; Comparison of proposed budget increases against inflation, population growth, and assessment growth; Historical trends in municipal tax increases and cumulative impacts on households; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED; That staff report annually on the affordability implications of the proposed budget and identify the impact of tax supported budget increases on the average household, And that the Household Affordability Framework be used as an advisory tool to support Council budget deliberations and long term financial planning.
motions.text_html:
Whereas municipal property taxes continue to represent a continual and growing expense for households, businesses, and and seniors living on fixed incomes,
And whereas, inflation is only one measure of affordability and does not fully reflect residents’ financial circumstances or their ability to absorb additional tax increases,
And whereas, the true ability to pay is influenced by household income growth, housing costs, utility costs, food prices, transportation expenses and others cost of living pressures,
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT:
Regional Council direct staff to develop and implement a “Household Affordability Framework” to be included annually as part of the Region’s budgeting process,
And that, the framework include where practical : Medium household income trends within the Region of Waterloo; Property tax burden as a percentage of household incomes; Cost of living indicators including housing, utilities, food, transportation, and insurance costs; Affordably impacts on seniors and residents living on fixed incomes; Comparison of proposed budget increases against inflation, population growth, and assessment growth; Historical trends in municipal tax increases and cumulative impacts on households;
AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED;
That staff report annually on the affordability implications of the proposed budget and identify the impact of tax supported budget increases on the average household,
And that  the Household Affordability Framework be used as an advisory tool to support Council budget deliberations and long term financial planning.
